newsitem.title: USA: IMF says Sri Lanka needs to step up reforms.
newsitem.headline: IMF says Sri Lanka needs to step up reforms.

text.p: Sri Lanka needs to strengthen its macroeconomic policies and step up the pace of structural reforms if it wants to exploit its full economic potential, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Tuesday.

Noting the improved outlook for the country's economy this year, the IMF Executive Board said: "The main challenge now...(is) to build on that success to make an urgent and comprehensive effort to strengthen macroeconomic policies and accelerate structural reforms."
Sri Lanka's economy grew by 3.8 percent last year, well below the average of most countries in the region. The IMF expects growth to pick up to around six percent this year.
The IMF said the country's high fiscal deficits had been a key source of its economic woes over the past years.

"Fiscal consolidation must therefore be the key ingredient in the adjustment strategy to stabilise the economy and improve its growth prospects," it said in a summary of its annual report on the country.

The fund said Sri Lanka needed to press ahead with structural reforms in several key areas. It said priority should be given to strengthening the banking sector, keeping up the pace of privatisation, reinvigorating trade reforms and promoting competitive market forces in agriculture.
"Directors stressed that it would be important to keep inflation well within the single-digit range. That would require a tight monetary policy stance," the IMF added.

Consumer price inflation in Sri Lanka has slowed to an annualized four percent in June from as much as 22 percent in September 1996, when food shortages and administrative price rises pushed up the index.
